Composite action and workflow hygiene, checked by code (cli-contract section 9).

- Every third-party `uses:` is pinned by a 40-character commit SHA with its release tag in a
  comment on the same line (local `./` references are exempt).
- Workflows pin the runner image: no `*-latest` labels.
- The action's shell steps contain no `${{ }}` expressions: inputs reach scripts through `env:`.
- The action is composite, declares exactly the documented inputs, and every one of them is
  named in docs/action.md.
- The minimal upload names files and the two report directories, never the whole output
  directory; retention defaults to 14 days; the full upload defaults to off.
- release-version.txt equals the package version (cognous_ocs.__version__ and pyproject.toml).

Claim-boundary checker (cli-contract section 10).

Fails if any tracked document, README, action text, source string or built wheel says
certified, compliant or production-ready (and close variants) while publication or
production is on HOLD per release-state.json. A missing or malformed release-state.json
counts as HOLD. Matches are excused only by an exact entry in
scripts/claim_boundaries_allowlist.json; an allow-list entry that no longer matches
anything is itself an error, so the list cannot rot.

Usage: check_claim_boundaries.py [--root DIR] [--wheel FILE ...]

Examples parity: bundled example fixtures are byte-equal to their recorded hashes.

Reads src/cognous_ocs/fixtures/<example>/ straight from disk (not through the package), so it also
catches a stray, missing or edited file before a wheel is built. With --source-dir it also
requires the files recorded as byte-equal to the hub example to match that checkout; the
default run is offline and needs no hub checkout.

Lock freshness: the `stack` extra pins equal cognous_ocs.lock, and any *.lock files agree.

The pins are the current component mains, which differ from the hub component-lock commits
until the hub lock is updated (see provenance.json and docs/demo.md). A stale or edited pin
fails. Each extra needs requirements/<extra>.txt naming every dependency it declares (regenerate with
uv, see docs/testing.md); any requirements*.lock file must mention every pinned commit.

Schema snapshot immutability check, and the one place a new snapshot is recorded.

`schemas/SNAPSHOTS.json` records the sha256 of every file in every `schemas/vN/` snapshot.

- every `schemas/vN/` directory is listed, with exactly the recorded files and hashes;
- every listed snapshot exists;
- for every git tag matching `v[0-9]*`, each `schemas/vN/` directory present at that tag is
